raw.transcript: First, restart your router by unplugging it for about 10 seconds, then plug it back in and wait until all the lights look normal. Next, on your computer or phone, forget the Wi-Fi network and reconnect by entering the password again. Third, move closer to the router to rule out weak signal or interference. Fourth, check for other devices causing interference, like cordless phones or microwaves, and move them away if possible. Fifth, update your router’s firmware and your device’s Wi-Fi drivers; you can usually find those options in the router’s admin page and your system updates. Sixth, if it still drops, try a different channel or band, like switching between 2 point 4 and 5 gigahertz, and if that doesn’t help, contact your internet provider to check for service issues or get a replacement router.
